units.notes: Aeneas does not model Vec capacity: alloc.vec.Vec.with_capacity _ n := Vec.new, so the capacity change itself (the only real difference: capacity of the returned Vec) is invisible in the model. However the old code still evaluates input.as_ref().len() * 4 with overflow checking (Aeneas = debug-build semantics) and panics when len*4 > usize::MAX (possible for slices of length in (usize::MAX/4, isize::MAX], e.g. >1 GiB inputs on 32-bit targets, debug builds only); the new code never computes it. Hence REFINES in the model (new more defined); in release builds (wrapping arithmetic) the two are EQUIV. 'Not conversely' is witnessed only on the old side (old = fail integerOverflow); whether new returns ok there depends on the user Engine impl and opaque Vec::as_mut_slice. Old also calls as_ref twice (once for the capacity hint, once in decode_engine_vec); the model treats AsRef::as_ref as a pure function, so this is harmless. Proof time ~20 min.

units.name: base64::encoded_size (private)
units.evidence: Proof.lean: encoded_size_not_equiv : Old.encoded_size 0#usize ≠ New.encoded_size 0#usize (old_zero: Old 0 = ok 4, new_zero: New 0 = ok 0; step*, kernel-checked); extraction tag esz, charon --start-from base64::encoded_size, no cargo args, no external axioms
units.notes: Deliberate change of a capacity hint: old = 4*(len - len%3)/3 + (len%3==0 ? 4 : 0) (over-estimates by 4 when len%3==0, UNDER-estimates by 4 otherwise, e.g. len=1: old 0, new 4); new = (len/3)*4 + (len%3==0 ? 0 : 4) = exact padded length. They differ for every len (old - new = +4 if len%3==0 else -4; only the len=0 counterexample is proved). Overflow domains also differ: old's 4*(len-rem) overflows (panic in Aeneas/debug semantics) for len > usize::MAX/4, new only near usize::MAX.

units.name: base64::encode_mode (and encode_mode_buf, same pattern)
units.evidence: Extraction OK (tag emode, --start-from base64::encode_mode; EmodeOld/EmodeNew typecheck), but encode_mode = String::with_capacity(encoded_size(len)) then encode_mode_buf (String::reserve(encoded_size(len)), String::as_mut_vec); these are opaque axioms `alloc.string.String.with_capacity : Usize → Result String`, `String.reserve : String → Usize → Result String`, `String.as_mut_vec`, and they receive different arguments (e.g. len=0: old with_capacity 4, new 0). Equivalence needs 'with_capacity/reserve ignore the capacity argument', which is not derivable and not assumed.
units.notes: In Rust semantics the capacity argument only affects allocation, so the API is expected to be EQUIV except for the overflow-panic domain: old encoded_size panics (debug) for len > usize::MAX/4 where new does not (new would be more defined). Not proved; no Lean proof attempted at api level. Primary verdict (api) = UNSUPPORTED; raw = NOT_EQUIV (intended capacity-hint change).

commits.notes: raw encoded_size NOT_EQUIV by design (encoded_size_not_equiv: 0 -> old 4 / new 0; secondary, private capacity hint). Primary api encode_mode: only the String capacity argument changes, but String::with_capacity/reserve/as_mut_vec are opaque axioms, so the user-visible equality cannot be established -> UNSUPPORTED(missing-std-model).
